concerns: The external Telegram API call is executed inside a @Transactional method, which holds a database connection open during network I/O and could lead to connection pool exhaustion under load.
The dailyLimit limit is hardcoded as a field (20) in the service class instead of being configurable via Spring environment properties.
Uses OffsetDateTime.now() directly in the application code, which can make testing sliding window time-sensitive logic brittle; injecting a Clock bean is preferred.
The external Telegram API call is executed inside a class-level @Transactional service method, holding the DB connection open during external network requests.
Uses LocalDateTime instead of OffsetDateTime or Instant, which does not store timezone information and can lead to rate limiting discrepancies if servers are deployed across different time zones.

The test class CampaignMessageDispatcherServiceTest relies on manual repository deletions in @BeforeEach instead of class-level @Transactional rollback, which can make the test environment more brittle.
